newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable despite riot news.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable despite riot news.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate late trading on Thursday despite reports of a riot in a small west Java town, dealers said.
A mob of Indonesian Moslems burned and wrecked churches and temples east of Jakarta on Thursday morning after reports that a Christian had insulted Moslems, officials said.
"The rampage was sparked by an (ethnic) Chinese woman who scolded a number youths for being too noisy," Dadang Muchtar, the head of the Karawang regency, told a news conference.
He said the mob wrecked four churches and a temple.
One U.S. bank dealer said liquidity expectations seemed to have turned around in the afternoon, with operators seen rushing to buy tom/next swaps which soared to 2.35 points.
They remained biddish at 2.2 points late in the afternoon, suggesting anticipation of tight liquidity on Friday.
"This is a surprise change," one Japanese bank dealer said.
PLayers were selling tom/next swaps earlier on anticipation of ample rupiah supply following operators' speculaion of large amounts of maturing short-term papers (SBIs) on Friday.
However, operators seemed to realise that Friday happened to be the month-end, the weekend and time for weekly tax payments.
Tom/next swaps fell earlier to 1.5 from 1.8 points.
Spot rupiah was at 2,373.20/73.50 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,371.5/72.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,370.75/71.25 and 2,370.50/71.00, respectively.
Dealers said rises in tom/next swaps helped drive longer-term rates to follow.
One-month swaps were at 12.20/13.00, two at 23.50/24.50, three at 36.50/38.00 and six at 73.50/75.00 points.
Overnight swaps remained expensive as operators seemed to make daily roll-overs to cover longer-term swap positions, one local bank dealer said.
He said many operators seemed to anticipate a possible injection of fresh rupiah if the central bank was forced to intervene to keep the dollar within its intervention band.
"If that happens again, swap premiums will fall. People seem to prepare for that scenario, causing short-term swaps to be more expensive than longer-term rates," the dealer said.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,371/2,563 and the conversion band at 2,371/2,419 on Thursday.
The central bank had depreciated the rupiah by two points this week and last week after lowering it by four points the previous week. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
